title: Floating-promise and unhandled-rejection policy

options.name: Keep current behaviour: no process handler, un-awaited calls stay as they are
options.risk: Any rejection on an un-awaited path (listener callbacks, pollers, the entry point, async intervals and close handlers) exits the process under Node 22 (exit 1); every exit monitor and anti-rug subscription stops until someone restarts the bot.

options.name: Contain every un-awaited entry with .catch that logs and alerts
options.behavior_impact: The process survives a failing handler; the failing handler's own work is abandoned with an alert.
options.risk: A half-finished buy or arming step can continue unnoticed if the escalation is only a log line; each new call site must remember the wrapper.

options.name: Add a process-level unhandledRejection handler that alerts and shuts down cleanly
options.behavior_impact: Unknown failures stop the bot on purpose; open positions are re-armed by the boot resume when it is restarted.
options.risk: Without an automatic restart, positions are unmonitored from the shutdown until the operator restarts.

options.name: Add a process-level handler that alerts and keeps running
options.behavior_impact: The bot never exits on a stray rejection.
options.risk: It keeps trading in an unknown state (for example a position whose arming failed half-way).

options.name: Both: contain per handler (fail closed for startup, listener and arming paths) and a global handler that alerts and shuts down cleanly
options.behavior_impact: Expected failures are contained where they happen; anything unexpected stops the bot with an alert.
options.risk: More code paths to test; same restart dependency as global-alert-shutdown for the unexpected case.

recommendation: contain-plus-global (research recommendation): contain each handler with a fail-closed escalation for startup, listener and arming paths, plus a global handler that hard-alerts and triggers a controlled shutdown; never disable no-floating-promises; do not add awaits inside event handlers or poll loops in lint-only commits.
default: Keep current behaviour until the owning phase decides (milestone contract). This card covers S0/S1 capital findings, which cannot rest on the default: until it is decided and fixed it blocks the live re-entry gate.
behavior_impact: Decides whether a stray async error crashes the bot, is contained, or stops it on purpose; affects every position's protection during an error.
needed_by: Phase 24 discussion (capital fixes, after the Phase 23 real-path proof)
